knowledge:
- key_parameters: formula=formula specifying the survival model (e.g., Surv(time, status) ~ predictors) ;; data=data frame containing the variables ;; weights=vector of case weights ;; subset=expression indicating which subset of rows to use
- alternatives: coxme=for mixed-effects Cox models ;; survminer=for advanced visualization of survival curves ;; eha=for alternative parametric models
- when_to_use: Appropriate when analyzing time-to-event data, particularly when censoring is present (right, left, or interval censoring), such as patient survival, time-to-recurrence, or equipment failure times.
- pitfalls: Failing to properly format time-dependent covariates (leading to immortal time bias) ;; ignoring the proportional hazards assumption in Cox models ;; misinterpreting the sign of coefficients in survreg (which models log-time) versus coxph (which models log-hazard).

workflows.name: kaplan_meier_survival_curves
workflows.intent: Estimate and plot non-parametric survival curves using the Kaplan-Meier method to compare survival times between groups.
input: patient_clinical_data.csv (clinical table containing survival time, survival status, and grouping factors like treatment or gender)
workflows.stages: 1. Define the survival outcome using Surv() ;; 2. Fit the Kaplan-Meier survival curve using survfit() ;; 3. Summarize survival probabilities and median survival times using summary() ;; 4. Plot the survival curves using plot().
workflows.code:
library(survival)
fit <- survfit(Surv(time, status) ~ sex, data = lung)
summary(fit)
plot(fit)

workflows.name: cox_proportional_hazards_regression
workflows.intent: Fit a semi-parametric Cox proportional hazards model to evaluate the effect of multiple continuous and categorical covariates on survival.
input: patient_clinical_data.csv (clinical table containing survival time, survival status, and multiple clinical covariates)
workflows.stages: 1. Fit the Cox proportional hazards model using coxph() ;; 2. Summarize hazard ratios and significance using summary() ;; 3. Test the proportional hazards assumption using cox.zph().
workflows.code:
library(survival)
fit <- coxph(Surv(time, status) ~ age + sex + ph.ecog, data = lung)
summary(fit)
cz <- cox.zph(fit)
print(cz)
